## Review: `dip/trail-list-filters-output`

The three commits rework `entire trail list` filters/output: replace `--all` with `--author`/`--status`/`--limit`, change the default to in-progress only, switch to grouped/dynamic-width output, and remove the title column. Direction looks good; new tests for `limitTrails`, `filterTrailsByAuthor`, `parseTrailStatusFilter`, and `printTrailList` are a nice addition. Two real bugs and a few smaller things to fix.

### Bugs

**1. `--author me` is broken — wrong endpoint and wrong field.** `cmd/entire/cli/trail_cmd.go:312`
```go
resp, err := client.Get(ctx, "/api/v1/me")
```
The BFF route is mounted at `/auth` (entire.io api: `app.ts:332` → `v1.route("/auth", authApiRoutes)` and `auth.ts:1175` → `authApiRoutes.get("/me", …)`), so the real path is `/api/v1/auth/me`. The request as written will 404 (handled as a generic error). Even if it didn't 404, the response shape is `{ id, github_login, … }` — there is no `login` key (`auth.ts:1265-1276`), so `currentUserResponse{Login string `json:"login"`}` would still decode empty and fall into the "current user response did not include a login" path. Net result: `--author me` cannot work in its current form. Fix by hitting `/api/v1/auth/me` and reading `github_login` (or add a real `login` field server-side).

There's no test exercising `fetchCurrentUserLogin` end-to-end, which is why this slipped through. Worth adding a unit test that stubs `*api.Client` against `/api/v1/auth/me`.

**2. `NoOptDefVal = ""` makes space-separated values silently disappear.** `cmd/entire/cli/trail_cmd.go:143-144`
```go
cmd.Flags().Lookup("author").NoOptDefVal = ""
cmd.Flags().Lookup("status").NoOptDefVal = ""
```
Once a flag has `NoOptDefVal`, pflag stops consuming the next argv token as its value. So `entire trail list --status open` parses as `--status=""` plus a positional `open` (silently ignored — `runTrailListAll` doesn't read args), and the user gets "any status" instead of "open". Same for `--author alice`. Only `--status=open` / `--author=alice` work. This is a real footgun given the help text doesn't mention it.

Options: drop `NoOptDefVal` and instead reserve a sentinel value like `--status any` / `--author any`, or keep `NoOptDefVal` and call `cmd.Args = cobra.NoArgs` plus document the `=` requirement. The sentinel route is friendlier.

### Smaller issues

**3. Padding width is bytes, not display columns.** `cmd/entire/cli/trail_cmd.go:393-401`
```go
branchWidth := len([]rune(t.Branch))   // measured in runes
…
fmt.Fprintf(w, "%-*s  %-*s  %s\n", branchWidth, t.Branch, …)  // padded in bytes
```
`fmt`'s `%-*s` pads by byte count, not runes/cells, so the rune-based `branchWidth` only helps if the branch is ASCII. Multi-byte (or wide) branch/author names will misalign. If alignment matters, compute width with `runewidth.StringWidth` and use a manual padding loop, or accept the misalignment and drop the rune measurement.

**4. Behavior change in `entire trail` (no subcommand) is silent.** `cmd/entire/cli/trail_cmd.go:75, 93` now pass `defaultTrailListStatus = "in_progress"` on the fallback path. Previously the fallback showed "everything except merged/closed". Now it shows in-progress only, with no UI hint that other statuses exist. That's a reasonable default but worth a note in `Long` text or commit message so users know `--status=` flips it off.

**5. Status-default discoverability.** `--help` will show `--status string  Filter by comma-separated status(es): … (default "in_progress")` plus mark it as a flag with optional value because of `NoOptDefVal`. The combination renders awkwardly and obscures that `in_progress` is the default. A short example line in the long description ("Show all statuses: `entire trail list --status=`") would help.

**6. Trails with an unknown status are silently dropped.** `trailListStatusOrder` enumerates known statuses; in the grouped path (`printTrailList` when `grouped == true`), trails whose `Status` isn't in that list never reach `printTrailRows`. Block on #1 (broken feature) and ideally fix #2 before merging — they together mean the new flags don't actually work the way the help text claims. The rest is polish.

package api

import (
	"time"

	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/trail"
)

// TrailListResponse is the response from GET /api/v1/trails/:org/:repo.
type TrailListResponse struct {
	Trails        []TrailResource `json:"trails"`
	RepoFullName  string          `json:"repo_full_name"`
	DefaultBranch string          `json:"default_branch"`
	UpdatedAt     time.Time       `json:"updated_at"`
}

// TrailResource represents a single trail from the API.
type TrailResource struct {
	Number          int              `json:"number,omitempty"`
	TrailID         string           `json:"trail_id"`
	Branch          string           `json:"branch"`
	Base            string           `json:"base"`
	Title           string           `json:"title"`
	Body            string           `json:"body"`
	Status          string           `json:"status"`
	Author          *trail.Author    `json:"author"`
	Assignees       []string         `json:"assignees"`
	Labels          []string         `json:"labels"`
	Priority        string           `json:"priority,omitempty"`
	Type            string           `json:"type,omitempty"`
	Reviewers       []trail.Reviewer `json:"reviewers,omitempty"`
	CreatedAt       time.Time        `json:"created_at"`
	UpdatedAt       time.Time        `json:"updated_at"`
	MergedAt        *time.Time       `json:"merged_at,omitempty"`
	CommentCount    int              `json:"comment_count,omitempty"`
	UnresolvedCount int              `json:"unresolved_count,omitempty"`
	CheckpointCount int              `json:"checkpoint_count,omitempty"`
	CommitsAhead    int              `json:"commits_ahead,omitempty"`
}

// ToMetadata converts a TrailResource to a trail.Metadata for display.
func (r *TrailResource) ToMetadata() *trail.Metadata {
	m := &trail.Metadata{
		Number:    r.Number,
		TrailID:   trail.ID(r.TrailID),
		Branch:    r.Branch,
		Base:      r.Base,
		Title:     r.Title,
		Body:      r.Body,
		Status:    trail.Status(r.Status),
		Author:    r.Author,
		Assignees: r.Assignees,
		Labels:    r.Labels,
		Priority:  trail.Priority(r.Priority),
		Type:      trail.Type(r.Type),
		Reviewers: r.Reviewers,
		CreatedAt: r.CreatedAt,
		UpdatedAt: r.UpdatedAt,
		MergedAt:  r.MergedAt,
	}
	if m.Assignees == nil {
		m.Assignees = []string{}
	}
	if m.Labels == nil {
		m.Labels = []string{}
	}
	return m
}

// TrailCreateRequest is the body for POST /api/v1/trails/:host/:owner/:repo.

## Second pass

Confirmed the two original bugs (I verified pflag source at `pflag/flag.go:994` — `NoOptDefVal != ""` skips next-arg consumption, so `--status open` really does parse as `--status="" open`; and the BFF mounts auth routes at `/api/v1/auth`, so `/api/v1/me` is a 404 and the right endpoint returns `github_login`, not `login`). Here are issues I didn't raise the first time.

### New findings

**1. New tests miss `t.Parallel()`.** `cmd/entire/cli/trail_cmd_test.go`
CLAUDE.md says "Always use `t.Parallel()` in tests. Every top-level test function and subtest should call `t.Parallel()` unless it modifies process-global state." None of these touch env/cwd/shared state, so each top-level test should add `t.Parallel()`. Convention isn't followed everywhere in this dir, but new code should set the bar.

**2. `runTrailListAll`'s signature is a footgun.** `cmd/entire/cli/trail_cmd.go:149`
```go
runTrailListAll(ctx, w, authorFilter, statusFilter string, jsonOutput bool, limit int, insecureHTTP bool)
```
Seven positional args with two `bool`s straddling an `int` and two adjacent `string`s. Adding `defaultTrailListLimit` and toggling `jsonOutput` at a call site is easy to silently mis-order — both `runTrailShow` call sites already pass `false, defaultTrailListLimit, insecureHTTP` and look like template magic. Wrap these in a `trailListOptions` struct.

**3. `--limit` doesn't limit the network call.** `entire.io/api/src/routes/trails.ts:471-579` accepts no `limit`/`status`/`author`/`since` query params. The CLI pulls every trail in the repo on every invocation and filters/limits locally. Fine for now, will hurt at scale; consider pushing filters to the BFF before this is unhidden.

**4. Author match is case-sensitive.** `filterTrailsByAuthor` at `trail_cmd.go:246-253` does `t.AuthorLogin() == login`. GitHub logins are case-insensitive — `--author=Alice` won't match author `alice`. The `me` path resolves via API so it's safe, but explicit logins can silently produce zero rows. `strings.EqualFold` would fix it.

**5. `trailListStatusOrder` silently drops unknown statuses in grouped output.** `trail_cmd.go:402-426` enumerates the known statuses; trails with any new server-issued status never appear in any group. Today all statuses are in the enum, but if the server adds one and the CLI is older, the trail vanishes from the grouped view (and from the count discrepancy might look like a bug). Append an "Other" bucket for unknown statuses, or emit a warning.

**6. "Recent trails · 1" doesn't pluralize.** `trail_cmd.go:362-365`
```go
if len(opts.StatusFilters) == 0 {
    fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Recent trails · %d\n", count)
```
The author/status header path calls `pluralize("trail", count)`, but this one hardcodes "trails". For count=1 the user sees "Recent trails · 1". Tiny, but inconsistent.

**7. Grouping heuristic deserves a comment.** `trail_cmd.go:340` — `grouped := len(opts.StatusFilters) != 1` is intentional (one explicit status means the status is already in the header, so flat is enough; zero or multi means group), but reads like an off-by-one. One-line comment would save a reader thirty seconds.

**8. JSON output silently honors the implicit `in_progress` default.** `trail_cmd.go:211-218` emits the filtered slice. Anyone scripting against `entire trail list --json` now gets only in-progress trails by default — a behavior change without a marker in the payload. Either document this in `--help` or have `--json` imply `--status=` unless explicit.

**9. The "Your trails" relabel branch is untested.** `trail_cmd.go:374-376` rewrites `RequestedAuthor` to "Your trails" when it equals `CurrentUser`. No test covers it; the existing author/status test passes `RequestedAuthor: "alice"` with no `CurrentUser`, so the substitution never fires. Add a row.

**10. `fetchCurrentUserLogin` runs after the trails list serially.** Two round-trips when one would do (`/me` could run concurrently with the trails fetch via `errgroup`). Minor latency cost, but `--author me` does feel slower than it should. Optional.

### Nits

- `defaultTrailListAuthor = ""` is referenced exactly twice in `runTrailShow`. Inlining `""` reads more honestly than naming an empty default.
- `NoOptDefVal = ""` on `--author` is dead code: the flag's static default is also `""`, so `--author` (bare) and not passing it at all are identical. Either remove `NoOptDefVal` on `--author`, or change the static default to something else so the "bare flag" syntax has a distinct meaning.
- Consider `-n` for `--limit` for parity with common CLI conventions.
- `branchWidth := len([]rune(t.Branch))` is rune-counted but used with `%-*s` which pads by bytes — already raised; one fix: use `text/tabwriter` instead of manual padding (handles tabs cleanly and avoids the rune/byte mismatch).

### Verdict (unchanged from first pass)

Still blocking on the `/api/v1/me` bug and the `NoOptDefVal`-eats-next-arg bug. The new structural points above (signature, server-side filtering, case sensitivity, JSON filtering, missing test coverage for "Your trails") are good follow-ups regardless.

## Third pass — after `f469b96f2 Resolve trail author me via GitHub CLI`

### What changed

`fetchCurrentUserLogin` no longer hits the BFF — it shells out to `gh api user --jq .login` via the existing `ghCurrentUser` helper. The bad `/api/v1/me` path and the `currentUserResponse{Login}` decode are gone. The error message now points users at `--author <login>` as a fallback when `gh` isn't available.

### Verdict on the first-pass blockers

**Bug #1 (wrong `/me` endpoint and field): fixed**, though I'd argue the better fix was hitting `/api/v1/auth/me` and reading `github_login`. Reasons below.

**Bug #2 (`NoOptDefVal` eats the next arg): unchanged.** `--status open` still parses as `--status="" open` and silently drops the filter. Still the more important of the two — I'd not merge without addressing it.

### New concerns introduced by this commit

**1. Identity drift between `entire` and `gh`.** The trail list is fetched with Entire's auth; "me" is resolved through GitHub's auth. They can disagree:

- Different GitHub accounts logged in (`gh auth switch` to a personal account, while the Entire session is your work identity).
- User has an Entire account that isn't linked to the `gh`-logged-in GitHub user at all.

In both cases `--author me` filters by *the gh user's* login, which is not what the user thinks they're asking for. The previous (broken) BFF call had the right intent. If the BFF can return `github_login` for the current Entire user, calling that is more correct than `gh api user`.

If you keep the `gh` route, at minimum surface the resolved login before filtering ("Filtering by your trails: alice") so the user can spot a mismatch.

**2. New hard dependency on `gh` for a single flag value.** Everything else in `entire trail` works against the BFF directly. Now one specific value (`--author me`) requires `gh` installed *and* authenticated *and* matching the right account. The fallback ("pass `--author <login>` explicitly") only fires on failure — there's no upfront discoverability. A line in the flag help would help: `... use 'me' (requires gh CLI) or a GitHub login`.

**3. `execRunner{}` is hardcoded, so the new code path isn't testable.** `trail_cmd.go:308` — `ghCurrentUser` accepts a `bootstrapRunner` interface specifically so callers can inject `fakeRunner` (see `setup_github_test.go:167`). The new wrapper kills that seam:
```go
func fetchCurrentUserLogin(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
    login, err := ghCurrentUser(ctx, execRunner{})
    ...
}
```
There's no test covering the new flow — the error wrapping, the empty-login branch, or the success case. Easy fix: pass the runner through, default to `execRunner{}` at the trail-list call site, and add two tests.

**4. Error context is fine but slightly long.** The wrapped message is:
```
resolve --author me: gh api user: <underlying>: (pass --author <login> explicitly if GitHub CLI is unavailable)
```
That nested `: ` chain reads awkwardly. Consider:
```
return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve --author %s via gh CLI: %w\nHint: pass --author <login> explicitly if gh is unavailable", trailListAuthorMe, err)
```
The newlined hint is friendlier than the inline parenthetical.

**5. `gh` is invoked even when an explicit `--author <login>` would have worked.** Right — only `authorFilter == trailListAuthorMe` triggers the call, so this is fine. Just confirming I checked.

### Still open from earlier passes (no change)

In rough priority order:

- `NoOptDefVal = ""` makes `--status open` / `--author alice` silently misbehave (space-separated value becomes a positional).
- New tests don't call `t.Parallel()`.
- `runTrailListAll` has a 7-arg signature with two bools straddling an int — should be a struct.
- Author match is case-sensitive (`strings.EqualFold` would fix it).
- Default `--status=in_progress` is invisible in JSON output (scripts may not notice the implicit filter).
- Branch column width uses runes but `fmt`'s `%-*s` pads by bytes.
- Unknown statuses silently disappear from grouped output.
- "Recent trails · 1" doesn't pluralize.
- "Your trails" relabel branch is untested.
- BFF accepts no `?status=`/`?author=`/`?limit=`, so the CLI pulls every trail and filters locally.
- Hidden `entire trail` (no subcommand) silently switched its default from "everything except merged/closed" to "in-progress only".

### Recommendation

Pick one of two paths and ship it:

1. **Keep the gh approach**: add a runner-injection seam + tests, document the gh dependency in `--author`'s help, and print the resolved login before filtering.
2. **Switch to `/api/v1/auth/me`** (BFF), read `github_login`. No new dependency, no identity drift, and you can add a test against an `httptest.Server`.

I'd take option 2 — it matches the rest of the trail command's posture (BFF-backed, single auth, easy to test) and avoids the identity-drift trap. Either way, please also fix the `NoOptDefVal` arg-parsing bug before this lands.
